_format: tools/date_rails.py output. features: { "<geojson id>" | "<id>/<piece>": {line, born, died, kind, basis, confidence, [from,to]} }. Split features are cut at vertex indices from..to. Edit tools/date_rails.py (LINES / THROUGH / SPLITS) and re-run, or edit this file directly.

extras.name: CPR to the Louise Bridge (gap)
extras.basis: joins feature 70 to feature 280 on the CPR route to the Louise Bridge (schematic)

extras.name: CPR over the Louise Bridge and east to the east-bank line
extras.basis: CPR trains used the Louise Bridge from 26 Jul 1881 (CBC/MHS); "Combination CPR/City Bridge until 1904" (City of Winnipeg). East connector is schematic.

extras.name: CNoR mainline over the Red River (Mill St to Rue Davreau)
extras.basis: Canadian Northern bridge over the Red, built with the line 1901-02 (MHS); Mill St (west) to Rue Davreau (east) per Mike; straight and schematic

cpr_louise.basis: CPR yards at Point Douglas and the line over the Louise Bridge: first CPR train into Winnipeg 26 Jul 1881 (CBC / MHS)

cpr_west.basis: CPR main line west, Winnipeg–Portage la Prairie, built direct in late 1881 (MHS, "Rails Across the Red")

cpr_yardtrk.basis: CPR Point Douglas yard tracks — yard dates from 1881, tracks added as traffic grew (spread to 1900)

cpr_eastbank.basis: CPR line east of the Red River (St. Boniface side): CPR trains came in from the east over the Louise Bridge from 26 Jul 1881 (CBC / MHS); the Point Douglas bridge that carries it across the river here is 1902

cpr_bridge.basis: CPR Red River bridge at Point Douglas and its approaches: built 1901–02, first train early July 1902 (MHS)

cpr_sw.basis: Pembina Mountain / Southwestern branch (Manitoba & South Western) — grading 1881, rails 1881–82 (MHS); identification of this line is a guess

cpr_weston.basis: CPR Weston yards and approaches — Weston shops/yards 1900s; no firm date found (spread 1903–1906)

npm_forks.basis: Northern Pacific & Manitoba line to the Forks / Water Ave station and shops, 1889 (MHS); later Canadian Northern East Yards

transfer.basis: Winnipeg Transfer Railway: company 1889, "about five years" to complete, joining the CPR at Point Douglas Ave to the NP&M at Water Ave

cnor_east.basis: Canadian Northern line east over its Red River bridge (built 1901–02, MHS); identification is a guess

gwwd.basis: Greater Winnipeg Water District Railway from St. Boniface (c.1913–1915); identification is a guess
